question: Should app-level explicit Claude OAuth recover through the authenticated Claude CLI only when safe direct credentials are absent, or should explicit OAuth remain terminal even for that absence?
rationale: This is a user-visible credential-authority and compatibility contract, not a mechanical implementation detail: the fallback can intentionally select the active Claude CLI account after an OAuth source was chosen.

options.title: Adopt owner-mediated recovery
options.body: Keep the OAuth-to-owner-CLI fallback for exact credential absence, after current-head live proof confirms it never reads Claude Code’s Keychain item and preserves account authority.

options.title: Keep OAuth terminal
options.body: Remove the fallback so users who explicitly choose OAuth receive a terminal recovery action instead of usage from the ambient Claude CLI account.

options.title: Defer the routing policy
options.body: Pause this PR until maintainers define the permanent explicit-OAuth recovery contract and its account-labeling expectations.

recommendation.title: Adopt owner-mediated recovery
recommendation.body: Keep the OAuth-to-owner-CLI fallback for exact credential absence, after current-head live proof confirms it never reads Claude Code’s Keychain item and preserves account authority.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the independent validation that exposed the test-safety and credential-boundary assumptions, making them the strongest evidence-backed routing candidate available in this review context.
